text: Several speakers, Mr Darryl David, Ms Mariam Jaafar, and Ms Hany Soh have asked to consider a differentiated regime for vocational drivers under the revised Driver Improvement Points System.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This was why we made sure to consult the transport unions while formulating this policy.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: They are the NTUC's affiliated associations, namely: the National Delivery Champions Association, the National Private Hire Vehicles Association, the National Taxi Association and the National Transport Workers' Union.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We considered carefully what it would mean if there were to be a differentiated regime for vocational drivers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This, in effect, creates a lower standard of road safety accountability for one group of road users versus the rest.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Seen in this light, it is very difficult to justify.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: That said, while we intend for the lower thresholds for licence suspension and revocation to nudge all motorists to adhere more closely to traffic rules in future, we agree it would be good to ease the transition wherever possible.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I am heartened that our transport unions have been proactive in championing road safety beyond just the Driver Improvement Points System changes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In particular, they have been speaking out against the dangers of being distracted on the roads, such as holding a handphone or watching videos while driving.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Just today, the NTWU as well as NTUC Assistant Secretary-General, Ms Yeo Wan Ling, who has been very helpful in facilitating MHA and Traffic Police's engagement with the unions, released a Facebook video to actively remind the vocational driver community that no notification, booking or message is worth the risk of a momentary lapse in attention that could cost lives.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar asked to consider a similar mechanism to Spain's points-based licensing system, where a sustained period without any offence may increase their threshold for suspension or revocation.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Kenneth Tiong made a similar suggestion and asked that the Traffic Police take into consideration one's driving history over a longer period of time.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I have explained that the one-time deduction of demerit points on 1 January 2027 is a transitionary measure, not intended to formalise another means of rewarding or incentivising safe driving behaviour.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We had considered introducing an additional buffer for drivers with good driving history.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But upon reflection, this seems to be at odds with our intention of resetting driving behaviour across a backdrop of a worsening road situation.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We think it is better to retain the existing incentives for good driving behaviour under the revised Driver Improvement Points System.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: These incentives reward sustained responsible driving behaviour and offer drivers an opportunity to rehabilitate their records.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We believe these incentives are effective and will be continued.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Darryl David, Ms Hazlina Halim, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Ms Hany Soh asked to consider introducing an early intervention course, refresher course or performance improvement plan for drivers, before they hit suspension.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: A similar mechanism had previously existed in the form of the Safe Driving Course, available to all drivers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: These findings suggest that introducing similar early intervention courses that allow reduction in demerit points are unlikely to contribute to the objectives of safer roads.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It is about ensuring that every person who uses our roads – whether motorist, rider, cyclist or pedestrian – can do so with greater safety and confidence.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Laws and enforcement are important but safer roads ultimately depend on the daily choices that each of us makes – to slow down, to stay alert, to put away distractions and to think of the other persons on the road.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We agree that laws must be evidence-based and this principle has guided several amendments in this Bill, such as the revised drink driving limits.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Members have raised other suggestions that go beyond the scope of the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: MHA and Traffic Police will work with the relevant agencies to consider these suggestions.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: For instance, suggestions relating to road infrastructure is something that we will discuss with LTA.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Also, suggestions to make platform workers' work environment safer can also be taken up at the Multi-Agency Task Force on Workplace Safety and Health, and this is a task force that the Traffic Police is very glad to be invited to recently by the Ministry of Manpower.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We also encourage our partners, including unions, transport and platform operators, and community organisations to step forward and do their part by reinforcing safe habits, supporting responsible driving and helping every road user make safer choices.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Once again, I thank Members for supporting the Bill.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
text: I appreciate that these applications can be case-by-case.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Looks like a very comprehensive rounding up speech.      .
